requirements.evidence: `.env.example:1` sets APP_NAME=PegaFila and `:7` APP_LOCALE=pt_BR, and `phpunit.xml:22-24` pins all three values. `config/mail.php:129-130` configures markdown theme `pegafila`, and `resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:240-244` paints `.button-primary` (present in both mails) with #0f7490; the CSS is Laravel's default theme with only the brand colors changed. `lang/pt_BR.json:559` and `:803` add the two notification subjects. `routes/web.php:16-32` defines all five named routes with `guest`, `throttle:6,1`, and `auth`+`signed`+`throttle:6,1`. `app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetLinkController.php:25-31` validates the e-mail and always returns the same `passwords.sent` status; `app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:31-50` validates token/e-mail/password (min 8, letters, mixed case, numbers, confirmed), rotates `remember_token`, fires `PasswordReset` and redirects to `/`; `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:14-18` fulfils the request and redirects to `/`; `app/Models/User.php:6,15` adds `MustVerifyEmail`.

conventions.evidence: Clear deviation: `app/Http/Controllers/NewPasswordController.php:31-35` uses inline `$request->validate()` for three fields including a composite Password rule, while conventions ask for a Form Request once rules go beyond one or two fields. Also `resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:1-31` and `reset-password.blade.php:1-42` are plain HTML with no Bulma classes or Blade components, unlike the project's UI convention (the task does allow any markup, so this is only a nit). Positives: the flows reuse Laravel's Password broker and built-in notifications instead of new layers (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:29`, `NewPasswordController.php:37-45`), the write uses `forceFill` (`NewPasswordController.php:40-43`), and `CHANGELOG.md:12` is updated.

security.evidence: Verification authorization is delegated to `EmailVerificationRequest` in `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:14`, which rejects id/hash mismatches with 403 (covered by `tests/Feature/EmailVerificationTest.php:30-73`). All input is validated server-side (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:25-27`, `NewPasswordController.php:31-35`). `password.email` returns the same flash whether or not the account exists, avoiding enumeration (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:29-31`). Every Blade echo uses `{{ }}` (`forgot-password.blade.php:18-26`, `reset-password.blade.php:19-38`), forms carry `@csrf`, and the password/remember-token write bypasses mass assignment via `forceFill` (`NewPasswordController.php:40-43`). No secrets or debug output in the diff.

tests.evidence: `tests/Feature/PasswordResetTest.php:14-117` covers form render, link sent, non-enumeration, e-mail validation, reset form render, successful reset with token rotation and `PasswordReset`, weak-password rejection and invalid token. `tests/Feature/EmailVerificationTest.php:11-73` covers the happy path, hash mismatch, another user's id and an unsigned link. `tests/Feature/AuthEmailsTest.php:10-56` covers the locale/name/theme config, the #0f7490 theme and both translated mails. Missing: a test that authenticated users are redirected by the `guest` middleware (`routes/web.php:16`) and a test for the required `throttle:6,1` limit on `password.email` (`routes/web.php:20`).

simplicity.evidence: The change reuses Laravel's built-in `ResetPassword`/`VerifyEmail` notifications and `Password` broker rather than custom classes (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:29`, `NewPasswordController.php:37-45`); the controllers are 33 and 57 lines with no service/repository layer, and the theme is a straight copy of Laravel's default CSS with the brand colors substituted (`pegafila.css:240-244`).

readability.evidence: Small, single-purpose methods with docblocks (`PasswordResetLinkController.php:14-32`, `NewPasswordController.php:16-56`, `VerifyEmailController.php:10-19`), names that mirror Laravel's auth scaffolding, consistent route grouping, and no dead code, commented-out blocks or debugging in the diff.

scope.evidence: Only task-relevant files are touched: `.env.example`, `phpunit.xml`, `config/mail.php`, `lang/pt_BR.json`, the two controllers, `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php`, `app/Models/User.php`, `routes/web.php`, the two views, the theme CSS, three test files and `CHANGELOG.md:12`. Nothing from the out-of-scope list (login/registration/logout, `/home`, verification notice/resend, Livewire, layouts, nginx/Docker, SCSS/JS) is added.

issues.explanation: Inline `$request->validate()` handles three fields (token, email, password) with a composite Password rule, whereas the project conventions require a Form Request once the rules grow beyond one or two fields.
No test exercises the `guest` middleware on the password routes (`routes/web.php:16`), so the task's guests-only requirement is implemented but not protected against regression.
The required `throttle:6,1` limit on `password.email` is never asserted, so it could be removed without any failing test.

The mail tests assert subject, greeting and action text but never assert that the action URLs target `password.reset`/`verification.verify`, although requirement 5 makes the notification URL part of the contract.
The two auth screens are plain unstyled HTML without Bulma classes or a shared Blade component, so they will look out of place in a Bulma project (mitigated by the task allowing any markup).

review.summary: The change delivers pt-BR password-reset and e-mail-verification e-mails using Laravel's built-in notifications, a PegaFila markdown mail theme, the five named routes/controllers/views, locale pins and thorough feature tests. All task requirements and the security posture hold up on a read-through; the main gaps are a three-field inline validation that the conventions would put in a Form Request and missing tests for the guest-only routes and the e-mail throttle.
